crisis communication is a “work in progress” and a “work in process” in the context of a changing administrative state.
crisis communication is a complex and challenging task for all involved in the public sector.
crisis communication is not only about the technical aspects of the communication but also about the political and social contexts in which it occurs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crisis-communication capabilities of public organizations and their political leaders are still not up to the task of responding to the demands of the public and the media during a major crisis.
crisis communication in the Neo-liberal context is increasingly privatized and commoditized.

the crisis communication vulnerability points are more than a matter of technology and information management.
the “crisis communication” field is still in its infancy, with little consensus on how to define the concept, let alone how to measure it.
